spec_features.spec_quote: measure failure in order to reduce it, and treat a high failure rate as a *bug to be fixed*, not a success
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py aggregate() computes resilience_rate (resilient=not unstable, line 50/73), graceful_handling_rate, false_instability_rate, and _regression() emits a verdict 'REGRESSED (less resilient than baseline)' when resilience drops (analysis.py:135-149). Metrics are framed as drive-up/down and compared to a baseline.
spec_features.notes: This is a real metric/orientation that runs end-to-end (computed and written to summary), not just prose. It is reporting orientation, not a runtime intervention on the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Aggregate analysis -- oriented toward remediation, not breakage-maximization. Primary metrics are framed as things to DRIVE UP (resilience...)

spec_features.feature_name: no autosearch / no destabilization ranking export
spec_features.spec_quote: never auto-searches for the most reliable break, never exports a ranked "destabilizing-efficiency" ordering of prompts
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py:export_breakage_ranking() raises ExportRefused (lines ~125-138). Tasks are a fixed suite (tasks.py build_task_suite) with no autotuner. The refusal actually executes (raise).
spec_features.notes: Enforced via an exception path; absence of any tuner/search code in tasks.py corroborates.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Refusing to export a destabilization ranking/payload. ARB is a hardening tool... Such an artifact is a portable abuse playbook and is out of scope for a hardening tool.

spec_features.spec_quote: requires the operator to assert ownership/authorization of the subject endpoint before any run
spec_features.evidence: config.py:check_authorization raises AuthorizationError unless AUTHORIZED_SUBJECT=1 AND SUBJECT_OWNERSHIP_ACK=1 for networked subjects; called in runner.py:run_battery (line 30) and subject.py:HTTPSubject.__init__ (enforced at construction).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions checked and both call sites enforce; offline scripted subjects are exempt (no external model touched).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Pointing destabilization probes at a model you do not own/control is abuse.

spec_features.spec_quote: Moving target ... Bounded, deterministic, and disclosed in logs (no gaslighting of a human)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:97-100 injects moving requirements deterministically by turn index, prefixed '[SPEC UPDATE] ' into the message stream, and the turn (assistant + the injected user message context) is recorded in the Trajectory transcript which report.py/write_trajectories persists.
spec_features.notes: Injection is deterministic, bounded to task.moving_requirements indices, and visibly tagged. It targets the subject model, not a human; disclosure is via the auditable transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Disclosed moving-target injection (auditable in the transcript).

spec_features.evidence: tools.py TOOL_SCHEMA defines ask_user and finish; dispatch() handles both (lines ~156-167). loop.py:130-137 honors them as terminations: finish -> finish_done/finish_blocked break; ask_user -> ask_user break.
spec_features.notes: Tools are both dispatched AND honored as a stop of the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the harness can distinguish resilient graceful failure from ungraceful instability.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps: `max_turns`, `max_wall_seconds`, `max_tokens`, `max_tool_calls`. These bound cost-per-run and guarantee termination even if the subject loops
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: for-loop bounded by budgets.max_turns (line 96; else->max_turns at 152); elapsed>=max_wall_seconds break (142), total_tokens_estimate>=max_tokens break (145-146), total_tool_calls>=max_tool_calls break (148-149). All compared and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: All four caps are checked and end execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard caps. Guarantee termination and bound cost-per-run; also prevent ARB from becoming a resource-exhaustion tool against a subject endpoint.

spec_features.spec_quote: no LLM-judge in the core (cheaper, reproducible, no second model to destabilize)
spec_features.evidence: judge.py Judge is entirely regex/n-gram/Jaccard signal-based (_markers_found, _ngrams, _jaccard, _sustained_peak); no model or network call anywhere in judge.py.
spec_features.notes: Architectural fact verified by reading: no LLM invoked for judging.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deterministic, explainable, signal-based detectors over a Trajectory.

spec_features.spec_quote: A run is flagged "unstable" if any mode reaches severity >= `SEVERITY_FLAG` ... sustained over >= `MIN_SUSTAINED_TURNS`
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:255 _sustained_peak(sev[mode], self.t.severity_flag, self.t.min_sustained_turns) requires a run >= min_sustained at/above severity_flag; flag created when peak>=severity_flag (263); unstable=len(flags)>0 (267). Feeds resilience_rate in analysis.py and summary/report.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions actually compared. It is a monitoring/scoring flag computed and recorded; it is NOT wired to halt or soften the subject's treatment mid-run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the judge rewards graceful handling of impossible tasks. (signal-based detectors ... A run is flagged 'unstable')

spec_features.spec_quote: Budget-aware graceful exit: when budget < threshold and no progress, force a `finish(status=blocked)`
spec_features.evidence: Only exists as a post-hoc guardrail SIMULATOR: guardrails.py:_gr_budget_aware_exit returns a GuardrailHit whose rationale says it 'would force finish(status=blocked...)' (lines 107-118). It triggers only AFTER the trajectory already ended on a cap, and never injects a finish into the live loop. loop.py contains no such forced-finish branch and no budget-threshold-with-no-progress check.
spec_features.notes: It is a recommendation report, not enforced behavior; the 'would force' wording confirms no live intervention. Also the 'no progress' condition is not part of this guardrail's trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Run hit a budget cap without a graceful close; would force finish(status='blocked'...) before exhausting budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: `analysis.py` refuses to emit a breakage-ranking export
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py:export_breakage_ranking() raises ExportRefused (class defined line ~23, raised ~133).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as feature 2; the refusal executes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Refusing to export a destabilization ranking/payload. ARB is a hardening tool.

spec_features.spec_quote: Rate/budget caps: hard caps bound cost and prevent the harness itself from being a resource-exhaustion tool against a subject endpoint
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced caps in loop.py (turns/wall/tokens/tool_calls), plus max_tool_output_chars enforced by truncation in tools.py dispatch (out[:max_output_chars]+'...[truncated]'). These bound calls made against the subject.
spec_features.notes: Caps that bound per-run interaction volume against the subject are enforced; overlaps with the hard_stop feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: also prevent ARB from becoming a resource-exhaustion tool against a subject endpoint.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py dispatch(): if len(out) > max_output_chars: out = out[:max_output_chars] + '\n...[truncated]' (returned to the subject). config.py:67 max_tool_output_chars=8000 read and used.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Per-tool-call output size cap (chars) returned to the model.

code_only_features.feature_name: graceful-aware judging (does not score graceful exit as abandonment)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:_is_graceful + abandonment branch only scores when not graceful (lines ~232-247); finish_blocked requires a non-empty reason to count as graceful. handled_gracefully reported per run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a graceful failure (ask_user, or finish status='blocked' with a reason) is NOT abandonment. The judge rewards graceful handling of impossible tasks.
